summary.text: 医 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 醫, used for medicine, healing, and physicians. A traditional dictionary interprets its graph as an arrow inside a weapon container, but early glyph evidence does not confirm that account.

formation.text: The received dictionary analysis treats 匸 as an enclosure for weapons and 矢 as an arrow within it, depicting a container for bows, crossbows, and arrows. A separate, disputed interpretation assigns 矢 a sound role.

components.text: In the received analysis, 匸 is the enclosure that stores or hides weapons. This historical dictionary interpretation is not independently confirmed by early glyph evidence.

In the received analysis, 矢 is the arrow inside the enclosure. A separate interpretation assigns it a sound role, but the cited readings do not establish that relation. The container’s name and pronunciation remain unknown.

sound_limitation.text: The cited readings do not establish the proposed 矢–医 sound relation; the name and pronunciation of the depicted container remain unknown.

sound.text: This current reading pair is descriptive and does not verify the proposed historical sound role.

history.text: The selected seal-script-style rendering of 医 shows 矢 within a frame-like 匸, matching the received dictionary analysis. It is a modern redraw of a historical script style, not a dated artifact or proof of the graph’s earliest form.

医 is listed as a variant of 醫 and is identified as its standardized simplified counterpart. This standardization does not establish when the forms became related or explain the earlier graphic history of 医.

uncertainties.text: The earliest dated occurrence and meaning of 医, and the precise graphic transition between 医 and 醫, remain unresolved. The weapon-container account is historical lexicographic testimony, not paleographic confirmation.
The proposed sound role of 矢 lacks a confirmed historical comparison. The evidence also does not establish that the whole graph 医 was borrowed to write the medical word.

senses.gloss: container for bows, crossbows, and arrows
senses.text: The received Shuowen entry gives this gloss and analyzes 医 as 匸 enclosing 矢. It is a historical dictionary account, not an independently confirmed earliest meaning.
医 is used for medicine, healing, and physicians. The evidence does not date these uses of 医 separately from its relationship to 醫.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish a semantic transition from the weapon-container gloss to medical meanings, or prove that 医 was borrowed as a whole character for the medical word because of sound.
Classical examples and dictionary glosses are available, but their dates and textual histories do not establish earliest attestation or a chronological sequence of senses.

evidence.text:
Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *qɯ): phonetic 殹 (OC *qiːs) + semantic 酉 (“liquor”).

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, Shuowen Jiezi entry for 医, with Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The entry glosses 医 as a container for bows, crossbows, and arrows, and analyzes it as 从匸从矢. Duan says 匸 hides/stores weapons and reports that the small-Xu version adds 矢亦聲, treating 矢 as a sound element as well as part of the analysis. Duan also notes the Guoyu quotation’s 医 is written 翳 in the received Guoyu text and discusses borrowing or extension involving the sense ‘conceal.’ This is a historical lexicographic account, not independent proof of an earlier inscriptional form or the depicted container’s name.
evidence.title: 說文解字「医」 - 「說文解字」在線查詢

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, entry 醫
evidence.text: The entry gives the Shuowen explanation that 醫 is a practitioner who treats illness, records the traditional analysis 从殹从酉, and preserves the alternative explanations that 殹 is an ‘ill appearance’ or a sound of illness and that alcohol is used in treatment. It lists the senses practitioner, medical art, and treatment, with examples from Xunzi, Han shu, Zhouli, Shiji, Mozi, and a Tang poem. It lists 医 among 醫’s variant forms. The entry supports the traditional relation but does not itself state here that 医 is the standardized simplified counterpart.
evidence.title: [A04248] 醫 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, entry 殹
evidence.text: The entry states that 殹 is analyzed in Shuowen as 从殳，医聲; it gives Mandarin yì and a secondary yī reading. Its senses include a sound associated with illness and a particle, with citations from Shuowen, Duan Yucai’s commentary, Qin inscriptions as reported by Duan, and a Mawangdui manuscript. This supports a phonetic component relationship between 殹 and 医 as described by the source, while leaving the original referent of the 医 shape and its sound history unresolved.
evidence.title: [C05910] 殹 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, Shuowen Jiezi entry for 医, with Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The entry glosses 医 as a container for bows, crossbows, and arrows, and analyzes it as 从匸从矢. Duan says 匸 hides/stores weapons and reports that the small-Xu version adds 矢亦聲, treating 矢 as a sound element as well as part of the analysis. Duan also notes the Guoyu quotation’s 医 is written 翳 in the received Guoyu text and discusses borrowing or extension involving the sense ‘conceal.’ This is a historical lexicographic account, not independent proof of an earlier inscriptional form or the depicted container’s name.

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants, entry 醫
evidence.text: The entry gives the Shuowen explanation that 醫 is a practitioner who treats illness, records the traditional analysis 从殹从酉, and preserves the alternative explanations that 殹 is an ‘ill appearance’ or a sound of illness and that alcohol is used in treatment. It lists the senses practitioner, medical art, and treatment, with examples from Xunzi, Han shu, Zhouli, Shiji, Mozi, and a Tang poem. It lists 医 among 醫’s variant forms. The entry supports the traditional relation but does not itself state here that 医 is the standardized simplified counterpart.

This supports a phonetic component relationship between 殹 and 医 as described by the source, while leaving the original referent of the 医 shape and its sound history unresolved.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

search_audit.query: site:shuowen.org/view/8380 医 矢亦聲 匸
search_audit.outcome: Opened the received Shuowen entry and inspected the gloss, component analysis, small-Xu sound note, and Duan commentary.

gaps: No direct, inspected early inscription image or dated attestation for either 医 or 醫 was obtained; claims about earliest attestation and the exact graphic transition remain unresolved.

The traditional Shuowen account of 医 and its analysis as 匸 plus 矢 is a historical lexicographic explanation, not independently confirmed here through paleographic evidence. Possible graphic corruption is not established by inspected primary forms.

The component account for 醫 preserves competing Shuowen explanations of 殹 and 酉; current evidence does not settle whether the 酉 explanation reflects original graphic motivation or later interpretation.

No exact local Baxter–Sagart rows exist for 医, 醫, 殹, 匸, or 殳. The exact row for 矢 is *l̥i[j]ʔ; this is not directly comparable to a reconstruction for 医 not found in the local dataset. Do not repeat an unverified secondary transcription as Baxter–Sagart data.
Modern Mandarin rows were locally checked for 医 and 醫, but official Unicode character-specific records were inaccessible. No local kMandarin row for the proposed components was supplied or relied on.

The sources support early lexicographic senses and cite classical usages, but this search did not verify the dates or textual histories of those works, nor establish a dated semantic chain from weapon container/cover to healer, medicine, and treatment.

No evidence of phonetic borrowing of the whole graph 医 for the medical word was established here. The medical character 醫 contains the physician/medical word in its own traditional form; the relation between its upper 殹 and the separate character 医 must not be conflated with a whole-graph loan claim.
No reuse terms were verified for any repeated source material; only concise character-specific paraphrases are reported.

No directly inspected dated oracle-bone, bronze, or manuscript attestation establishes the earliest occurrence of 医 or 醫, their earliest senses, or the graphic transition between them. The Shuowen entry is a received historical lexicographic interpretation, not paleographic confirmation.

No independent source establishes the depicted weapon-container's ancient name or pronunciation. The dossier's proposed whole-graph loan relationship between 医 and the medical word is unproven; do not infer a loan from similar present-day readings.

The traditional Shuowen accounts of 醫 conflict over 殹 (ill appearance versus illness sound) and explain 酉 through alcohol in treatment; no inspected early form resolves whether these reflect original graphic motivation or later interpretation.

The sound component account for 醫 is not established by a local Baxter–Sagart comparison: the dataset has no exact rows for 醫, 殹, or 医. Its exact 矢 and 酉 rows are not readings for 医 or 醫 and cannot independently prove those phonetic/semantic roles.

The required official Unicode Unihan character pages were unavailable in the earlier attempts recorded in the dossier. Local exact rows are provided as local checks only; current readings are not evidence for ancient sound relations.
The search did not verify dates or textual transmission of cited classical passages; lexicographic sense lists cannot establish chronological semantic development.

No verified early artifact glyph image was obtained. Commons candidates are modern redrawings of the Shuowen seal-style form. The original SVG retrievals failed in the web tool; candidate identity, page provenance, and stated reuse terms were inspected, but image pixels were not inspected by this researcher.
The repository does not provide evidence of bulk-reuse terms for repeated dictionary material; no local extract is recommended.
No directly inspected dated early artifact form or dated earliest attestation for 医 or 醫 was obtained; graphic development and earliest sense chronology remain unresolved.

The Shuowen weapon-container account for 医 and its component analysis are not independently confirmed by an early glyph image. No independent source establishes the container’s ancient name or pronunciation, so a whole-graph phonetic loan explanation for medical 醫 is unsupported.

The cited small-Xu phonetic interpretation of 矢 in 医 remains disputed. Current Mandarin readings shǐ/yī are not evidence of the historical sound relation, and the available local Baxter–Sagart table has no exact row for 医.
Official Unicode Unihan records for U+77E2 and U+533B could not be opened. The local exact readings were checked but no external Unicode click-through is claimed.
The sources preserve divergent historical explanations for 殹 and 酉 in 醫; inspected material does not settle their original motivation or establish a dated semantic chain from weapons to medicine.
The search did not verify the dating or transmission of cited classical examples as earliest attestations.

Official Unicode character-specific Unihan pages were not accessible in this session. Current reading pairs are supported by the provided exact local rows, not by inspected Unicode click-through pages.

The current Mandarin pair 矢 shǐ / 医 yī does not establish the small-Xu historical phonetic proposal. No exact Baxter–Sagart reading for 医 was provided, so the historical comparison remains unresolved.

The Shuowen gloss and small-Xu phonetic note are historical dictionary testimony, not independent evidence for the earliest form or pronunciation of the depicted container. Its original name and sound remain unrecovered.

The exact original SVG for 医-seal.svg could not be fetched by the web tool; its identity, source links, and stated reuse terms were verified on the exact Commons description page. The 醫 image's original link was available on its exact page.
No dated early artifact glyph or independently dated earliest medical or weapon-container use was established in this research pass; graphic development and semantic chronology remain unresolved.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern vector redraw of a received historical script form, not a dated artifact
items.caption: This seal-script-style rendering shows 矢 within a frame-like 匸, matching the received Shuowen analysis of 医 as a container for bows, crossbows, and arrows. That historical interpretation is not independently confirmed by an early glyph.
items.alt: A seal-script-style 医, with an arrow-like form inside a rounded, open-sided enclosure.
items.selection_reason: It directly illustrates the form and component analysis behind the entry’s disputed weapon-container explanation, while the caption keeps that account distinct from paleographic proof.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public-domain dedication stated on the Commons description page.

limitations.text: The selected image is a modern redraw of a received seal-script-style form, not a dated artifact. The other candidate depicts 醫 and adds no early evidence for 医 or for the graphic transition between them; the earliest form and that transition remain unresolved.
